## Objective
- Complete and smooth the Formula 1 history game.
- Make races longer than three laps, require a pit stop, and display elapsed race time.

## Requirements
- Cover Formula 1 history from 1950–2026 with career progression and race modes.
- Use mobile-friendly controls and lightweight procedural graphics without external game assets.
- Treat era stats as gameplay archetypes; historical driver and team names are contextual tributes.
- Support realistic speeds and circuit lengths, custom track drawing, mobile controls, rotation, and camera angles.
- Pit stops should change tyres and refuel when needed; races should require a pit stop, exceed three laps, and show a race timer.

## Decisions
- Use a static browser app with procedural graphics and synthesized engine audio.
- Use Three.js WebGL for race presentation, with a 2D fallback.
- Integrate Track Lab with the existing procedural track and race architecture.

## Work State
### Completed
- Implemented and browser-verified realistic circuit lengths, speed profiles, and AI acceleration/braking.
- Added Track Lab for drawing, naming, sizing, saving, and racing custom circuits.
- Reorganized mobile controls and prevented race-view page scrolling.
- Added race-view rotation and five camera modes; added showroom rotation controls.
- Added a pit-stop mini-game with four tyre changes, conditional refuelling, timing feedback, stop-time display, and pit-lane time loss.
- Browser-tested pit service and a three-lap race with a pit stop; fixed a recursive `updateAICars` stack overflow encountered during testing.
- Changed race/championship session length from three laps to five in `game.js`.

### Active
- Enforce a mandatory pit stop before race completion; the lap-boundary patch was attempted but not applied because its exact-text match failed.
- Add an elapsed-race-time HUD in `index.html`, update it from `game.js`, and make it visible on mobile in `styles.css`.
- Resolve the undefined `mergeStatic` call in `race3d/car.js`.
- Update the Race Day and Championship selectors from “3 laps” to match the new race length.
- Validate syntax and browser behavior, including a full race with mandatory pit stop; reassess reported low test-environment performance (~3.2 FPS).

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Inspect the current lap-boundary code in `game.js` and implement mandatory pit enforcement, ensuring the player cannot finish before completing a pit stop.
2. Add and update a separate elapsed-race-time HUD; retain existing lap timing and ensure mobile visibility.
3. Fix or remove the undefined `mergeStatic` call in `race3d/car.js`.
4. Update session selector labels, then run syntax and browser checks, including a full race and mandatory pit stop.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: Session setup, lap progression, pit-stop logic, elapsed time, and HUD updates.
- `index.html`: Race HUD and session selector; Race Day currently says “3 laps.”
- `styles.css`: Race HUD responsive rules; mobile currently hides `.time-box`.
- `race3d/car.js`: Procedural car construction calls undefined `mergeStatic(...)`.

## Important Context
- Current session lengths: qualifying 1 lap; practice and time trial 2 laps; race/championship now 5 laps.
- `g.elapsed` advances during racing and includes pit-lane penalty time; the existing `time-box` is lap timing (`p.lapTime`), not elapsed race time.
- The attempted mandatory-pit edit failed because the exact source text did not match; the existing lap logic still services only requested stops and finishes at the final lap.
- Changes from the latest work are uncommitted; no validation was run after changing the race lap count.
- Camera modes are CHASE, COCKPIT, TV, HELI, and ORBIT; cycle with `C` or select with `1–5`.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Complete and smooth the Formula 1 history game, including longer races, mandatory pit stops, and elapsed race-time display.

## Requirements
- Cover Formula 1 history from 1950–2026 with career progression and race modes.
- Use mobile-friendly controls and lightweight procedural graphics without external game assets.
- Treat era stats as gameplay archetypes; historical driver and team names are contextual tributes.
- Support realistic speeds and circuit lengths, custom track drawing, mobile controls, rotation, and camera angles.
- Pit stops should change tyres and refuel when needed; races should require a pit stop, exceed three laps, and show a race timer.

## Decisions
- Use a static browser app with procedural graphics and synthesized engine audio.
- Use Three.js WebGL for race presentation, with a 2D fallback.
- Integrate Track Lab with the existing procedural track and race architecture.

## Work State
### Completed
- Implemented and browser-verified realistic circuit lengths, speed profiles, and AI acceleration/braking.
- Added Track Lab for drawing, naming, sizing, saving, and racing custom circuits.
- Reorganized mobile controls and prevented race-view page scrolling.
- Added race-view rotation and five camera modes; added showroom rotation controls.
- Added a pit-stop mini-game with four tyre changes, conditional refuelling, timing feedback, stop-time display, and pit-lane time loss.
- Browser-tested pit service and a three-lap race with a pit stop; fixed a recursive `updateAICars` stack overflow encountered during testing.
- Changed race/championship session length from three laps to five in `game.js`.

### Active
- Validate the new mandatory pit-stop enforcement edits in `game.js`; race/championship now trigger a stop at the first lap boundary if `!g.pitCompleted`, and prevent finishing without one.
- Finish elapsed-race-time HUD integration; `#elapsedValue` initialization was added in `game.js`, but the HUD update edit failed to match, and markup is unconfirmed.
- Fix or remove the undefined `mergeStatic` call in `race3d/car.js`.
- Update Race Day and Historic Championship selector labels and lap-count HUD to reflect five laps.
- Run syntax and browser checks, including a full race with mandatory pit stop; reassess reported low test-environment performance (~3.2 FPS).

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Inspect `game.js` pit completion flow and verify mandatory service, lap progression, and race finish behavior.
2. Add elapsed-race-time HUD markup in `index.html`, update it during the race, and ensure it remains visible on mobile.
3. Fix the undefined `mergeStatic` call in `race3d/car.js`.
4. Update session selector and initial lap display to match five laps, then run syntax and browser validation.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: Session setup, lap progression, pit-stop logic, elapsed time, and HUD updates.
- `index.html`: Race HUD and session selector labels.
- `styles.css`: Race HUD responsive rules; mobile currently hides `.time-box`.
- `race3d/car.js`: Procedural car construction calls undefined `mergeStatic(...)`.

## Important Context
- Current session lengths: qualifying 1 lap; practice and time trial 2 laps; race/championship 5 laps.
- `g.elapsed` advances during racing and includes pit-lane penalty time; the existing `time-box` is lap timing (`p.lapTime`), not elapsed time.
- Mandatory-stop edits set `g.pitCompleted=true` when pit service finishes; this flow has not been validated after the latest changes.
- Changes are uncommitted; validation has not been run after the latest edits.
- Camera modes are CHASE, COCKPIT, TV, HELI, and ORBIT; cycle with `C` or select with `1–5`.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Complete and smooth the Formula 1 history game, including longer races, mandatory pit stops, and elapsed race-time display.

## Requirements
- Cover Formula 1 history from 1950–2026 with career progression and race modes.
- Use mobile-friendly controls and lightweight procedural graphics without external game assets.
- Treat era stats as gameplay archetypes; historical driver and team names are contextual tributes.
- Support realistic speeds and circuit lengths, custom track drawing, mobile controls, rotation, and camera angles.
- Pit stops should change tyres and refuel when needed; races should require a pit stop, exceed three laps, and show a race timer.

## Decisions
- Use a static browser app with procedural graphics and synthesized engine audio.
- Use Three.js WebGL for race presentation, with a 2D fallback.
- Integrate Track Lab with the existing procedural track and race architecture.

## Work State
### Completed
- Implemented and browser-verified realistic circuit lengths, speed profiles, and AI acceleration/braking.
- Added Track Lab for drawing, naming, sizing, saving, and racing custom circuits.
- Reorganized mobile controls and prevented race-view page scrolling.
- Added race-view rotation and five camera modes; added showroom rotation controls.
- Added pit-stop mini-game with four tyre changes, conditional refuelling, timing feedback, stop-time display, and pit-lane time loss.
- Browser-tested pit service and a three-lap race with a pit stop; fixed a recursive `updateAICars` stack overflow encountered during testing.
- Changed race/championship sessions to five laps.
- Added race-time HUD markup and update/reset logic; made the timer visible on mobile.
- Updated Race Day and Historic Championship selector labels and initial lap HUD to five laps.
- Removed the undefined `mergeStatic(...)` call in `race3d/car.js`.
- Ran `node --check game.js`, `node --check race3d/car.js`, and `node --check race3d/index.js` successfully.

### Active
- Validate mandatory pit-stop enforcement, lap progression, and finish behavior after the latest edits.
- Run browser checks, including a full race with mandatory pit stop; reassess reported low test-environment performance (~3.2 FPS).

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Browser-test a five-lap Race Day session, verifying a mandatory stop occurs and the player can finish after service.
2. Verify elapsed race time updates during racing and includes pit-lane penalty time on desktop and mobile.
3. Investigate performance if the reported low frame rate persists.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: Session setup, lap progression, pit-stop logic, elapsed time, and HUD updates.
- `index.html`: Race HUD and session selector labels.
- `styles.css`: Race HUD responsive rules, including mobile elapsed-time styling.
- `race3d/car.js`: Procedural car construction; undefined static-mesh merge call was removed.

## Important Context
- Current session lengths: qualifying 1 lap; practice and time trial 2 laps; race/championship 5 laps.
- `g.elapsed` advances during racing and includes pit-lane penalty time; the existing `time-box` is lap timing (`p.lapTime`), not elapsed time.
- Mandatory-stop edits trigger service at the first lap boundary without a completed stop and block finishing at the final lap boundary; this flow has not yet been validated after the latest changes.
- Changes are uncommitted in `game.js`, `index.html`, `styles.css`, and `race3d/car.js`.
- Camera modes are CHASE, COCKPIT, TV, HELI, and ORBIT; cycle with `C` or select with `1–5`.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Complete and smooth the Formula 1 history game, including longer races, mandatory pit stops, and elapsed race-time display.

## Requirements
- Cover Formula 1 history from 1950–2026 with career progression and race modes.
- Use mobile-friendly controls and lightweight procedural graphics without external game assets.
- Treat era stats as gameplay archetypes; historical driver and team names are contextual tributes.
- Support realistic speeds and circuit lengths, custom track drawing, mobile controls, rotation, and camera angles.
- Pit stops should change tyres and refuel when needed; races should require a pit stop, exceed three laps, and show a race timer.

## Decisions
- Use a static browser app with procedural graphics and synthesized engine audio.
- Use Three.js WebGL for race presentation, with a 2D fallback.
- Integrate Track Lab with the existing procedural track and race architecture.

## Work State
### Completed
- Implemented and browser-verified realistic circuit lengths, speed profiles, and AI acceleration/braking.
- Added Track Lab for drawing, naming, sizing, saving, and racing custom circuits.
- Reorganized mobile controls and prevented race-view page scrolling.
- Added race-view rotation and five camera modes; added showroom rotation controls.
- Added pit-stop mini-game with four tyre changes, conditional refuelling, timing feedback, stop-time display, and pit-lane time loss.
- Browser-tested pit service and a three-lap race with a pit stop; fixed a recursive `updateAICars` stack overflow encountered during testing.
- Changed race/championship sessions to five laps.
- Added race-time HUD markup and update/reset logic; made the timer visible on mobile.
- Updated Race Day and Historic Championship selector labels and initial lap HUD to five laps.
- Removed the undefined `mergeStatic(...)` call in `race3d/car.js`.
- Added mobile styling for the elapsed race clock.
- `node --check` passes for `game.js`, `race3d/car.js`, and `race3d/index.js`.

### Active
- Validate mandatory pit-stop enforcement, lap progression, and finish behavior after the latest edits.
- Browser-test a five-lap Race Day session, verifying a mandatory stop occurs and the player can finish after service.
- Verify elapsed race time updates during racing and includes pit-lane penalty time on desktop and mobile.
- Investigate performance if the reported low frame rate (~3.2 FPS) persists.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Use the available headless Chromium session to test a five-lap Race Day session, mandatory pit service, and finish behavior.
2. Check elapsed-time display and pit penalty time on desktop and mobile viewport sizes.
3. Reassess frame rate and inspect the final diff.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: Session setup, lap progression, pit-stop logic, elapsed time, and HUD updates.
- `index.html`: Race HUD and session selector labels.
- `styles.css`: Race HUD responsive rules, including mobile elapsed-time styling.
- `race3d/car.js`: Procedural car construction; undefined static-mesh merge call was removed.

## Important Context
- Session lengths: qualifying 1 lap; practice and time trial 2 laps; race/championship 5 laps.
- `g.elapsed` advances during racing and includes pit-lane penalty time; `time-box` is lap timing (`p.lapTime`), not elapsed time.
- Mandatory-stop edits trigger service at the first lap boundary without a completed stop and block finishing at the final lap boundary; this flow has not yet been validated after the latest changes.
- Pit service adds `PIT_LANE_LOSS` (18.5 seconds) plus stop time to elapsed and lap timing.
- Changes remain uncommitted in `game.js`, `index.html`, `styles.css`, and `race3d/car.js`.
- Camera modes are CHASE, COCKPIT, TV, HELI, and ORBIT; cycle with `C` or select with `1–5`.
- A local HTTP server and headless Chromium with remote debugging were started for browser testing, but no new browser validation has been completed.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Complete and smooth the Formula 1 history game, including longer races, mandatory pit stops, and elapsed race-time display.

## Requirements
- Cover Formula 1 history from 1950–2026 with career progression and race modes.
- Use mobile-friendly controls and lightweight procedural graphics without external game assets.
- Treat era stats as gameplay archetypes; historical driver and team names are contextual tributes.
- Support realistic speeds and circuit lengths, custom track drawing, mobile controls, rotation, and camera angles.
- Pit stops should change tyres and refuel when needed; races should require a pit stop, exceed three laps, and show a race timer.

## Decisions
- Use a static browser app with procedural graphics and synthesized engine audio.
- Use Three.js WebGL for race presentation, with a 2D fallback.
- Integrate Track Lab with the existing procedural track and race architecture.

## Work State
### Completed
- Implemented and browser-verified realistic circuit lengths, speed profiles, and AI acceleration/braking.
- Added Track Lab for drawing, naming, sizing, saving, and racing custom circuits.
- Reorganized mobile controls and prevented race-view page scrolling.
- Added race-view rotation and five camera modes; added showroom rotation controls.
- Added pit-stop mini-game with four tyre changes, conditional refuelling, timing feedback, stop-time display, and pit-lane time loss.
- Fixed recursive `updateAICars` stack overflow encountered during testing.
- Changed race/championship sessions to five laps and updated selectors and initial lap HUD.
- Added elapsed race-time HUD and mobile styling.
- Removed undefined `mergeStatic(...)` call in `race3d/car.js`.
- Browser-simulated a five-lap Race Day session through the first-lap mandatory pit stop to the finish; verified tyre service, 21.0-second penalty added to elapsed time, lap progression, and result screen.
- Verified elapsed-time display is visible within a 390×844 mobile viewport.
- `node --check` passes for `game.js`, `race3d/car.js`, and `race3d/index.js`; `git diff --check` passes.

### Active
- Investigate reported low frame rate (~3.2 FPS); headless Chromium logged software-WebGL stalls, so performance on hardware-accelerated browsers remains unverified.
- Inspect final diff.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Profile race rendering on a hardware-accelerated browser/device and address low frame rate if reproducible.
2. Review the final diff and remaining pit/fuel edge cases.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: Session setup, lap progression, pit-stop logic, elapsed time, and HUD updates.
- `index.html`: Race HUD and session selector labels.
- `styles.css`: Race HUD responsive rules, including mobile elapsed-time styling.
- `race3d/car.js`: Procedural car construction.
- `race3d/index.js`: Three.js race renderer.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted in `game.js`, `index.html`, `styles.css`, and `race3d/car.js`.
- Session lengths: qualifying 1 lap; practice and time trial 2 laps; race/championship 5 laps.
- Race/championship pit service triggers at the first lap boundary if not already completed, and finishing is blocked until service; the five-lap flow was browser-simulated successfully.
- Pit service adds `PIT_LANE_LOSS` (18.5 seconds) plus stop time to elapsed and lap timing.
- The tested stop did not require refuelling; conditional refuelling remains unverified in a complete browser race.
- Camera modes are CHASE, COCKPIT, TV, HELI, and ORBIT; cycle with `C` or select with `1–5`.

- Complete and smooth the Formula 1 history game, including longer races, mandatory pit stops, elapsed race-time display, and investigate reported low frame rate.

## Requirements
- Cover Formula 1 history from 1950–2026 with career progression and race modes.
- Use mobile-friendly controls and lightweight procedural graphics without external game assets.
- Treat era stats as gameplay archetypes; historical driver and team names are contextual tributes.
- Support realistic speeds and circuit lengths, custom track drawing, mobile controls, rotation, and camera angles.
- Pit stops should change tyres and refuel when needed; races should require a pit stop, exceed three laps, and show a race timer.

## Decisions
- Use a static browser app with procedural graphics and synthesized engine audio.
- Use Three.js WebGL for race presentation, with a 2D fallback.
- Integrate Track Lab with the existing procedural track and race architecture.

## Work State
### Completed
- Implemented and browser-verified realistic circuit lengths, speed profiles, AI acceleration/braking, and Track Lab for drawing, sizing, saving, and racing custom circuits.
- Reorganized mobile controls and prevented race-view page scrolling; added race-view rotation and five camera modes plus showroom rotation.
- Added pit-stop mini-game with four tyre changes, conditional refuelling, timing feedback, stop-time display, and pit-lane time loss.
- Fixed recursive `updateAICars` stack overflow and removed undefined `mergeStatic(...)` call in `race3d/car.js`.
- Changed race/championship sessions to five laps; practice/time trial are two laps and qualifying one lap.
- Added elapsed race-time HUD and mobile styling.
- Browser-simulated a five-lap Race Day session through a mandatory first-lap pit stop and finish; verified tyre service, 21.0-second pit penalty in elapsed time, lap progression, and result screen.
- Browser-simulated conditional refuelling through race finish; verified refuel to 32.1 L, pit completion, elapsed time, and results.
- `node --check` passes for `game.js`, `race3d/car.js`, and `race3d/index.js`; `git diff --check` passes.

### Active
- Investigate reported low frame rate on hardware-accelerated browser/device if available.
- Finish reviewing the current diff.

### Blocked
- Hardware-accelerated profiling remains unavailable; headless profiling is dominated by software WebGL and logged `GPU stall due to ReadPixels`.

## Next Move
1. Profile race rendering on hardware-accelerated hardware and address low frame rate if reproducible.
2. Finish reviewing the diff and rerun checks.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: Session setup, lap progression, pit-stop and fuel logic, elapsed time, and HUD updates.
- `index.html`: Race HUD and session selector labels.
- `styles.css`: Race HUD responsive rules, including mobile elapsed-time styling.
- `race3d/car.js`: Procedural car construction.
- `race3d/index.js`: Three.js race renderer, quality selection, and performance adaptation.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted in `game.js`, `index.html`, `styles.css`, and `race3d/car.js`.
- Mandatory pit service triggers at the first lap boundary if not already completed; finishing is blocked until service.
- Refuelling is staged only when `p.fuel < lapsLeft*7+2`; target fuel is based on remaining laps.
- Camera modes are CHASE, COCKPIT, TV, HELI, and ORBIT; cycle with `C` or select with `1–5`.
- Performance tests in headless Chromium do not establish hardware-accelerated performance.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Complete and smooth the Formula 1 history game, including longer races, mandatory pit stops, elapsed race-time display, and investigating reported low frame rate.

## Requirements
- Cover Formula 1 history from 1950–2026 with career progression and race modes.
- Use mobile-friendly controls and lightweight procedural graphics without external game assets.
- Treat era stats as gameplay archetypes; historical driver and team names are contextual tributes.
- Support realistic speeds and circuit lengths, custom track drawing, mobile controls, rotation, and camera angles.
- Pit stops should change tyres and refuel when needed; races should require a pit stop, exceed three laps, and show a race timer.

## Decisions
- Use a static browser app with procedural graphics and synthesized engine audio.
- Use Three.js WebGL for race presentation, with a 2D fallback.
- Integrate Track Lab with the existing procedural track and race architecture.

## Work State
### Completed
- Implemented and browser-verified realistic circuit lengths, speed profiles, AI acceleration/braking, and Track Lab for drawing, sizing, saving, and racing custom circuits.
- Reorganized mobile controls and prevented race-view page scrolling; added race-view rotation, five camera modes, and showroom rotation.
- Added pit-stop mini-game with four tyre changes, conditional refuelling, timing feedback, stop-time display, and pit-lane time loss.
- Fixed recursive `updateAICars` stack overflow and removed undefined `mergeStatic(...)` call in `race3d/car.js`.
- Set race/championship sessions to five laps; practice/time trial to two laps and qualifying to one lap.
- Added elapsed race-time HUD and responsive mobile styling.
- Browser-simulated five-lap Race Day through a mandatory first-lap pit stop and finish; verified tyre service, 21.0-second pit penalty in elapsed time, lap progression, and results.
- Browser-simulated conditional refuelling through race finish; verified refuel to 32.1 L, pit completion, elapsed time, and results.
- Latest `node --check game.js`, `node --check race3d/car.js`, `node --check race3d/index.js`, and `git diff --check` all pass.

### Active
- Review the current diff for regressions in mandatory pit-stop logic and race timer placement.
- Investigate the reported low frame rate on hardware-accelerated browser/device if available.

### Blocked
- Hardware-accelerated profiling remains unavailable; headless profiling is dominated by software WebGL and logged `GPU stall due to ReadPixels`.

## Next Move
1. Review the current diff, especially mandatory pit logic and timer placement.
2. Profile race rendering on hardware-accelerated hardware and address low frame rate if reproducible.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: Session setup, lap progression, pit-stop and fuel logic, elapsed time, and HUD updates.
- `index.html`: Race HUD and session selector labels.
- `styles.css`: Race HUD responsive rules, including mobile elapsed-time styling.
- `race3d/car.js`: Procedural car construction; removed invalid `mergeStatic(...)` call.
- `race3d/index.js`: Three.js race renderer, quality selection, and performance adaptation.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted in `game.js`, `index.html`, `styles.css`, and `race3d/car.js`.
- Mandatory pit service triggers at the first lap boundary if not already completed; finishing is blocked until service.
- Refuelling is staged only when `p.fuel < lapsLeft*7+2`; target fuel is based on remaining laps.
- Camera modes are CHASE, COCKPIT, TV, HELI, and ORBIT; cycle with `C` or select with `1–5`.
- Current diff moves `g.elapsed` accumulation until after race countdown; pit penalty time is added directly to elapsed time.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Complete and smooth the Formula 1 history game, including longer races, mandatory pit stops, elapsed race-time display, and investigating reported low frame rate.

## Requirements
- Cover Formula 1 history from 1950–2026 with career progression and race modes.
- Use mobile-friendly controls and lightweight procedural graphics without external game assets.
- Treat era stats as gameplay archetypes; historical driver and team names are contextual tributes.
- Support realistic speeds and circuit lengths, custom track drawing, mobile controls, rotation, and camera angles.
- Pit stops should change tyres and refuel when needed; races should require a pit stop, exceed three laps, and show a race timer.

## Decisions
- Use a static browser app with procedural graphics and synthesized engine audio.
- Use Three.js WebGL for race presentation, with a 2D fallback.
- Integrate Track Lab with the existing procedural track and race architecture.

## Work State
### Completed
- Implemented and browser-verified realistic circuit lengths, speed profiles, AI acceleration/braking, and Track Lab for drawing, sizing, saving, and racing custom circuits.
- Reorganized mobile controls and prevented race-view page scrolling; added race-view rotation, five camera modes, and showroom rotation.
- Added pit-stop mini-game with four tyre changes, conditional refuelling, timing feedback, stop-time display, and pit-lane time loss.
- Fixed recursive `updateAICars` stack overflow and removed undefined `mergeStatic(...)` call in `race3d/car.js`.
- Set race/championship sessions to five laps; practice/time trial to two laps and qualifying to one lap.
- Added elapsed race-time HUD and responsive mobile styling.
- Browser-simulated five-lap Race Day through a mandatory first-lap pit stop and finish; verified tyre service, 21.0-second pit penalty in elapsed time, lap progression, and results.
- Browser-simulated conditional refuelling through race finish; verified refuel to 32.1 L, pit completion, elapsed time, and results.
- Reviewed the latest diff for pit-stop and timer logic; no new regression identified.
- `node --check game.js`, `node --check race3d/car.js`, and `git diff --check` pass.

### Active
- Investigate the reported low frame rate on hardware-accelerated browser/device if available.

### Blocked
- Hardware-accelerated profiling remains unavailable; headless profiling is dominated by software WebGL and logged `GPU stall due to ReadPixels`.

## Next Move
1. Profile race rendering on hardware-accelerated hardware and address low frame rate if reproducible.
2. Keep the existing uncommitted changes intact while continuing.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: Session setup, lap progression, pit-stop and fuel logic, elapsed time, and HUD updates.
- `index.html`: Race HUD and session selector labels.
- `styles.css`: Race HUD responsive rules, including mobile elapsed-time styling.
- `race3d/car.js`: Procedural car construction; removed invalid `mergeStatic(...)` call.
- `race3d/index.js`: Three.js race renderer, quality selection, and performance adaptation.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted in `game.js`, `index.html`, `styles.css`, and `race3d/car.js`.
- Mandatory pit service triggers at the first lap boundary if not already completed; finishing is blocked until service.
- Refuelling is staged only when `p.fuel < lapsLeft*7+2`; target fuel is based on remaining laps.
- Camera modes are CHASE, COCKPIT, TV, HELI, and ORBIT; cycle with `C` or select with `1–5`.
- Race elapsed time accumulates after countdown starts racing; pit penalty time is added directly to elapsed time.
